text:
Strong margins against random negatives do not establish fine-grained next-item discrimination. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; repeated draws measure sampling variability but do not eliminate sampling bias. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds aggregate accuracy conceals head/mid/tail disparities, with random negative sampling favoring head items. These findings support examining candidate difficulty and popularity separately from the pinned host HR@10.

Proposed diagnostic synthesis: freeze each category’s BERT4Rec checkpoint; reconstruct next-item queries from public training prefixes using appended-mask inference, excluding the target from input. Repeatedly draw 99 unique unseen distractors under three diagnostic conditions: uniform, target-frequency-matched, and title/description similarity using local TF-IDF or token overlap without pretrained weights. Report target-rank distributions, HR@10 hit frequency across draws, target score minus the tenth-highest distractor score, and the fraction of queries switching across the rank-10 boundary. Stratify by target frequency and history length. Candidate-draw variability measures sensitivity to candidate composition, not calibrated preference uncertainty; training-prefix results are in-sample diagnostics.

Treat text-similar items as distractors with unknown relevance, rather than verified negatives: [Hard-BPR research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) highlights false-negative risks in hard mining. Frequency matching helps test whether success persists among similarly popular alternatives; lexical distractors probe discrimination among related descriptions, with limited semantic coverage. These are proposed audits, not a validated BERT4Rec diagnostic standard. Keep host validation unchanged and use metadata solely to construct audit pools; predictions retain exactly one trained model per category.
